segments.note: THE OPENER. The sand spit running out into the water with people walking it and the far shore behind. Nothing else in the library looks like this - it is the one stop that reads as open lake rather than a raft-up, which is the reason the Dam is on the stop list at all.
Paddleboarder and pontoons under a full Texas cloudscape. Same clip, 24s later - the sandbar sequence runs clean from 8s to 36s.

segments.note: A football caught mid-air against the clouds. The only action beat at this stop and the only frame in 143 seconds where something is thrown - worth the interruption. Spot-checked at source: the catch is at 122.8s exactly, so the window starts 1.8s before it rather than 3.3s - a one-second event should not arrive two thirds of the way into its own shot.

Boats rafted with a beach umbrella up, an orange float out and people standing between the hulls. Moved off 24s after a spot check: 24-32s is a run of close-ups of two guests, and the wide is at 18-23s.
FOURTH OF JULY. A stage and banners set up on the sandbar with the crowd standing in the water watching. This is a real event at this stop and it is the strongest argument the Dam has.
Same stage, later, with the crowd and boats filling the frame. Verified at 25.9s.
THE CLOSE. Open water, boats spread out, people standing in the shallows - back to the wide the cut opened on.
